title: The Gap Mathlib Leaves Open
content: Mathlib's Chebyshev file proves only the unweighted sum inequality, where the multiplier on the right is the cardinality #s. There is no weighted analogue in the library. This file supplies it: replace the uniform weight 1 by an arbitrary nonnegative weight w, and the cardinality #s by the total mass W = ∑ wᵢ. Setting w ≡ 1 recovers the Mathlib form exactly, so the weighted statement is a strict generalization rather than a separate result.
mathContext: $$\Big(\sum_{i\in s} w_i f_i\Big)\Big(\sum_{i\in s} w_i g_i\Big) \le \Big(\sum_{i\in s} w_i\Big)\sum_{i\in s} w_i f_i g_i, \qquad W := \sum_{i\in s} w_i.$$

title: Namespace and Variable Setup
content: Everything lives in the ChebyshevSumWeighted namespace with Finset open. The data is a finite index set s : Finset ι and three real-valued functions: the weight w and the two sequences f, g. Keeping ι an arbitrary type (rather than Fin n) means the results apply to sums over any finite index family. A LinearOrder on ι is introduced later, only for the monotone-sequence corollaries.

title: Sign of the Cross Difference (Monovary)
content: This is the one place monotonicity enters the whole development. By trichotomy on g i versus g j, the monovariance hypothesis forces f to move in the same direction as g: if g i < g j then f i ≤ f j, so both factors of (f i − f j)(g i − g j) are ≤ 0 and their product is ≥ 0; if g j < g i the signs flip together; the equal case kills the second factor. The proof discharges each branch with nlinarith fed an explicit product of nonnegative differences.

title: Sign of the Cross Difference (Antivary)
content: The mirror image of the monovary lemma. When f and g antivary, an increase in g forces a decrease in f, so the two factors carry opposite signs and the cross product is ≤ 0. Because the only difference from the monovary case is which inequality the predicate supplies, the entire reverse Chebyshev inequality downstream becomes a one-line sign flip rather than a re-derivation.

title: The Weighted Monovariance (Covariance) Identity
content: The algebraic heart of the file, and the part absent from Mathlib. The symmetric double sum ∑ᵢ∑ⱼ wᵢwⱼ(fᵢ−fⱼ)(gᵢ−gⱼ) expands into four monomial double sums; each one collapses via Finset.sum_mul_sum into a product of two single sums, and the four products recombine into exactly twice the Chebyshev defect W·∑ wfg − (∑ wf)(∑ wg). Crucially this identity uses NO hypothesis on the data — it is a pure rearrangement valid for arbitrary reals, which is why the inequality reduces entirely to controlling the sign of the summand.
mathContext: $$\sum_{i}\sum_{j} w_i w_j (f_i - f_j)(g_i - g_j) = 2\Big(W\sum_i w_i f_i g_i - \big(\sum_i w_i f_i\big)\big(\sum_i w_i g_i\big)\Big).$$

title: The Weighted Chebyshev Sum Inequality
content: The headline result. Combine the two ingredients: with nonnegative weights wᵢ, wⱼ ≥ 0 and each cross difference ≥ 0 (the monovary sign lemma), every summand of the double sum is nonnegative, so the double sum is ≥ 0 (positivity). Rewriting that nonnegative quantity via the monovariance identity and dividing by 2 gives the inequality. This is the lemma Mathlib lacks; the entire monotonicity content is quarantined in the sign lemma, so the analytic core is just 'a sum of nonnegative terms is nonnegative'.
mathContext: $$\Big(\sum_i w_i f_i\Big)\Big(\sum_i w_i g_i\Big) \le \Big(\sum_i w_i\Big)\sum_i w_i f_i g_i.$$

title: The Reverse (Antivary) Inequality
content: For antivarying f, g the cross differences are ≤ 0, so the weighted double sum is ≤ 0 and the same identity yields the reversed bound: W·∑ wfg ≤ (∑ wf)(∑ wg). The proof is structurally identical to the forward case with sum_nonpos in place of sum_nonneg and the antivary sign lemma, demonstrating how cleanly the sign of one factor propagates to the direction of the whole inequality.
mathContext: $$\Big(\sum_i w_i\Big)\sum_i w_i f_i g_i \le \Big(\sum_i w_i f_i\Big)\Big(\sum_i w_i g_i\Big).$$

title: Monotone-Sequence Corollaries
content: The open question is phrased for monotone sequences, not abstract monovariance. With a LinearOrder on ι, the bridges MonotoneOn.monovaryOn and MonotoneOn.antivaryOn convert 'both monotone' into 'monovary' and 'monotone vs antitone' into 'antivary'. The corollaries are then one-line compositions of those bridges with the main theorems — the named, user-facing forms the problem asks for.

title: Weighted Cauchy–Schwarz / Variance Bound
content: Because every function monovaries with itself (monovaryOn_self), specializing the main inequality to f = g costs nothing and yields a weighted square bound (∑ wf)² ≤ W·∑ wf². This is a weighted Cauchy–Schwarz / power-mean inequality and, read probabilistically, says the weighted variance E[f²] − E[f]² (scaled by W) is nonnegative. It holds for ANY f, with no monotonicity assumption, since self-monovariance is automatic.

title: Recovering Mathlib's #s Form
content: Substituting the constant weight w ≡ 1 collapses W = ∑ 1 = #s and ∑ 1·fᵢgᵢ = ∑ fᵢgᵢ, so the weighted bound becomes exactly Mathlib's (∑ f)(∑ g) ≤ #s · ∑ fg. This is the sanity check that the generalization is faithful: the new result contains the old one as a special case rather than diverging from it.

title: Worked Numerical Instance
content: A concrete check using the square bound with weights 1, 2, 3 against the sequence 0, 1, 2: the left side is (1·0 + 2·1 + 3·2)² = 8² = 64 and the right side is (1+2+3)·(1·0² + 2·1² + 3·2²) = 6·14 = 84, so 64 ≤ 84. The first example invokes weighted_sq_sum_le directly; the second discharges the fully evaluated numeric inequality by norm_num, confirming the abstract theorem produces correct numbers.
